reason: The source diff adds a real UnassignedExchange neighborhood to CVRP and VRPTW local search and changes move selection to prefer feasible priority increases before travel-cost gains. This is a solver search strategy, not a data-model or parameter edit.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: On capacity-constrained instances with unassigned high-priority single jobs, exchanging one assigned job for an unassigned job may raise served priority and improve lexicographic solution quality, but may increase local-search work or travel cost.
causal_chain: The new operator enumerates compatible unassigned single jobs against assigned route jobs, tests priority gain and capacity or time-window validity, then replaces a route job and updates the unassigned set. The global move loop now prioritizes a positive priority gain before distance gain, changing search trajectory and runtime.
structural_trigger: At least one compatible unassigned single job whose priority exceeds that of a route job, with a feasible replacement in CVRP or VRPTW; instances with all jobs assigned or equal priorities are controls.
activation_probe: On pinned Base and PR builds, record unassigned-job counts, compatible exchange candidates, validity rejections, positive-priority moves applied, route cost and served-priority changes; include a control without unassigned jobs.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze capacity-constrained CVRP and VRPTW panels with explicit job priorities and unassigned jobs before hidden scoring; stratify by priority skew, compatibility and time windows, and retain no-trigger controls, fixed seeds and all failures.
workload_exposure_plan: Use the shared VROOM anytime driver with priority-bearing input instances, trace the new operator on public cases, and independently verify returned original routing solutions and served-job priority.
mathematical_risk: An exchange can drop or duplicate a job, violate vehicle capacity or time windows, misstate served priority, or loop excessively if move invalidation is wrong.
independent_check_plan: Check each route against the original job set, uniqueness, capacity, time windows, priority total, and travel cost; compare quality-time trajectories across priority and no-priority panels.
hidden_generalization_plan: Compare paired served-priority and travel-cost trajectories on held-out CVRP and VRPTW instances with shifted priority distributions and capacity tightness, reporting family-level regressions.
overlap_review: This 2020 priority-aware unassigned exchange precedes VROOM #978 TSP fix and #1222 insertion bound at distinct snapshots. CVRP and VRPTW operator implementations are one PR and one task, with activation analyzed by family.
resource_risk: Enumerating extra unassigned-route exchanges can increase move checks and memory, while priority-first moves can increase distance or later repair work.
